flagged.title: Character Analysis: The Birlings
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly attributes the Act 3 quote 'I am ashamed of you' to Sheila both on-screen and in the voiceover, which is a mark-affecting quotation attribution error in a GCSE literature exam.

mark_affecting.quote: looking right at her parents and declaring 'I'm ashamed of you'

flagged.title: Key Themes
flagged.reason: The voiceover states the chain of events out of chronological sequence, claiming Mrs Birling denied Eva charity before Eric got her pregnant.

mark_affecting.quote: Sybil Birling coldly denied her charity, and Eric got her pregnant and stole to support her.

flagged.title: Exam Technique & Key Quotations
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly defines AO4 as assessing literary terminology (dramatic irony, stage directions, symbolism) when AO4 only assesses SPaG and vocabulary/sentence structure for clarity, misleading students into focusing effort on terminology that is not assessed.

mark_affecting.quote: crucially, it rewards you for using subject-specific literary terminology. When you drop in terms like dramatic irony, stage directions, or symbolism correctly to explain Priestley's methods, you are literally racking up AO4 points.
